iconic_games_note: NRG Stadium (opened as Reliant Stadium, 2002) has a genuine football (soccer) history as a regular USMNT and Mexico (El Tri) host venue: it hosted Copa América Centenario matches in June 2016 (the Argentina 4–0 USA semi-final on June 21, 2016, where Messi's free kick made him Argentina's all-time top scorer; plus group games), 2007 CONCACAF Gold Cup matches, and high-attendance USA–Mexico fixtures (70,103 in Feb 2008; a sellout 69,582 in May 2003). It is also a marquee non-football venue: NFL Super Bowls XXXVIII (2004) and LI (2017, Patriots 34–28 OT comeback over Atlanta), the 2024 College Football Playoff National Championship, WrestleMania 25 (2009), and the annual Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo. The 2026 World Cup is its first men's World Cup. NOTE: the original facts sheet mis-dated the Argentina–USA semi-final as June 11; the correct date is June 21, 2016.

city_history.significance: Founded August 30, 1836 by New York real-estate speculators Augustus C. and John K. Allen on land along Buffalo Bayou, and named for Texas Revolution hero (and later Republic of Texas president) General Sam Houston. It briefly served as capital of the Republic of Texas. Houston grew into the fourth-largest city in the United States (population exceeding 2.3 million; metro over 7 million), the global capital of the energy/oil-and-gas industry, home of NASA's Johnson Space Center (earning the nickname 'Space City'), the Texas Medical Center, and one of America's most ethnically diverse major cities.
city_history.football_culture: Houston is a strong soccer market anchored by MLS side Houston Dynamo FC (and NWSL's Houston Dash) at Shell Energy Stadium, and by a large, passionate Mexican-American fan base that has made the city a frequent host for the Mexico national team (El Tri) and CONCACAF events. NRG/Reliant Stadium has long been a go-to U.S. venue for USMNT–Mexico fixtures, Gold Cup, and Copa América Centenario matches, regularly drawing 68,000+ crowds.

stadium_history_facts: Groundbreaking March 9, 2000; topped off October 2001; construction completed in 30 months at a cost of US$352 million.
Opened August 24, 2002 with a preseason game (Miami Dolphins 24–3 over Houston Texans); first regular-season NFL game Sept 8, 2002 (Texans 19–10 over Dallas Cowboys).

First NFL facility with a retractable roof — two fabric panels split at the 50-yard line, openable in as little as 7 minutes; designed using kinetic-architecture principles by Populous (HOK Sport), Walter P Moore and Uni-Systems.
Co-tenant Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo (RodeoHouston) is integral to the design — the building was built 'as much for the rodeo as for the NFL.'
Originally named Reliant Stadium; became NRG Stadium in 2014 (NRG Energy naming rights). Renamed 'Houston Stadium' for the 2026 World Cup; Reliant name to be restored after the tournament.

Field surface history: natural-grass tray system at opening; permanent artificial turf installed 2015 (UBU Speed / Act Global), later Hellas Matrix Helix; temporary natural grass installed for the 2026 World Cup.
Has over 7,000 club seats, 186 luxury suites; regular capacity 72,220 (expandable to ~80,000 for special events).
Host venue for Super Bowls XXXVIII (2004) and LI (2017), 2024 College Football Playoff National Championship, and WrestleMania 25 (2009).
